items.q: Per capita income may be defined as
o: average earnings per head of population, often taken as a rough sign of living standards
the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods
the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared
anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth
items.s: Per capita income: average earnings per head of population, often taken as a rough sign of living standards. The other options describe Base year, Capital accumulation, Money.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Contractionary fiscal policy?
o: the fraction of an extra naira of earnings that households devote to buying goods and services
the outcome in which households trying to set aside more end up with lower total earnings and no more put by
the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training
a deliberate shrinkage of the deficit, through lighter public works or heavier taxation, meant to cool an overheated economy
items.s: Contractionary fiscal policy: a deliberate shrinkage of the deficit, through lighter public works or heavier taxation, meant to cool an overheated economy. The other options describe Marginal propensity to consume, Paradox of thrift, Underemployment.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Demand deposit.
o: the level of total spending that actually calls forth production and so settles how many people are employed
joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity
a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer
the extra worth a firm creates by working on goods and materials bought in from others
items.s: Demand deposit: a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer. The other options describe Effective demand, Value added, Cyclical unemployment.

items.q: Inflation may be defined as
o: the branch of study that examines the whole economy, its total output, total employment and general price level
the worth of output produced by the residents of a country, wherever they happen to be located
a sustained rise in the general level of prices that reduces the purchasing power of money
the buying or selling of government securities by the monetary authority in order to alter reserves
items.s: Inflation: a sustained rise in the general level of prices that reduces the purchasing power of money. The other options describe Macroeconomics, Open market operation, Gross national product.

items.q: The statement “anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth” describes which of the following?
o: Money
Demand deposit
Fiat money
Legal tender
items.s: Money is anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Monetary policy?
o: the shortfall in planned spending that leaves production below the level needed for full employment
expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests
action by the central authority to influence the cost and availability of credit and the quantity of money
the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training
items.s: Monetary policy: action by the central authority to influence the cost and availability of credit and the quantity of money. The other options describe Sustainable growth, Deflationary gap, Underemployment.

items.q: Liquidity may be defined as
o: an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else
spending that households go on undertaking even when their current earnings have fallen to nil
the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth
the expansion of deposits that occurs when lenders pass on a portion of what they receive
items.s: Liquidity: the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth. The other options describe Autonomous consumption, Intermediate good, Credit creation.

items.q: All of the following belong to Fiscal and monetary policy EXCEPT
o: Contractionary fiscal policy
Investment
Fiscal policy
Expansionary fiscal policy
items.s: Every other option belongs to Fiscal and monetary policy. “Investment” belongs to Consumption, saving and investment, not Fiscal and monetary policy.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Lender of last resort?
o: the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere
total earnings at which planned spending just equals what is produced, so that nothing pushes it to change
the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels
rising prices that originate in higher wages and higher input charges rather than in extra spending
items.s: Lender of last resort: the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere. The other options describe Cost-push inflation, Stabilisation policy, Equilibrium level of income.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Sustainable growth?
o: the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth
the difference between the worth of a country's exports and its imports of goods
the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending
expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests
items.s: Sustainable growth: expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests. The other options describe Trade balance, Multiplier, Liquidity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Underemployment?
o: the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training
the difference between the worth of a country's exports and its imports of goods
the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it
expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests
items.s: Underemployment: the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training. The other options describe Trade balance, Sustainable growth, Full employment.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Business cycle?
o: the institution that issues currency, holds the reserves of other lenders and acts as banker to the state
the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
the sum of all earnings accruing to the owners of land, labour, capital and enterprise in a period
the recurring movement of activity through expansion, peak, contraction and trough
items.s: Business cycle: the recurring movement of activity through expansion, peak, contraction and trough. The other options describe National income, Central bank, Double counting.

items.q: Full employment may be defined as
o: the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
the extra worth a firm creates by working on goods and materials bought in from others
the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it
the movement of spending and receipts between households, firms, the state and the rest of the world
items.s: Full employment: the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it. The other options describe Value added, Gross domestic product, Circular flow of income.

items.q: The statement “the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices” describes which of the following?
o: Inflation
Deflation
Phillips curve
Cost-push inflation
items.s: Phillips curve is the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices.

items.q: The statement “the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared” describes which of the following?
o: Expenditure approach
Real output
Non-market production
Base year
items.s: Base year is the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Public debt?
o: the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere
the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices
the accumulated obligations of the state to lenders at home and abroad
items.s: Public debt: the accumulated obligations of the state to lenders at home and abroad. The other options describe Phillips curve, Lender of last resort, Double counting.

items.q: Stagflation may be defined as
o: the combination of stagnant production and high joblessness with fast-rising prices
the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
the institution that issues currency, holds the reserves of other lenders and acts as banker to the state
a sustained rise in the general level of prices that reduces the purchasing power of money
items.s: Stagflation: the combination of stagnant production and high joblessness with fast-rising prices. The other options describe Gross domestic product, Inflation, Central bank.

items.q: Credit creation may be defined as
o: the expansion of deposits that occurs when lenders pass on a portion of what they receive
the proportion of deposits that lenders are obliged to keep in liquid form with the monetary authority
the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods
the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere
items.s: Credit creation: the expansion of deposits that occurs when lenders pass on a portion of what they receive. The other options describe Capital accumulation, Cash reserve requirement, Lender of last resort.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cyclical unemployment?
o: a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending
joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity
the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth
the branch of study that examines the whole economy, its total output, total employment and general price level
items.s: Cyclical unemployment: joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity. The other options describe Expansionary fiscal policy, Liquidity, Macroeconomics.

items.q: Which of the following best describes National income?
o: the sum of all earnings accruing to the owners of land, labour, capital and enterprise in a period
the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
currency that circulates because the state declares it acceptable rather than because of its material worth
a built-in feature such as a progressive tax that dampens swings in demand without any fresh decision
items.s: National income: the sum of all earnings accruing to the owners of land, labour, capital and enterprise in a period. The other options describe Double counting, Automatic stabiliser, Fiat money.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Open market operation.
o: the level of total spending that actually calls forth production and so settles how many people are employed
the record of all dealings between residents of a country and the rest of the world in a period
the buying or selling of government securities by the monetary authority in order to alter reserves
expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests
items.s: Open market operation: the buying or selling of government securities by the monetary authority in order to alter reserves. The other options describe Effective demand, Balance of payments, Sustainable growth.

items.q: The statement “the combination of stagnant production and high joblessness with fast-rising prices” describes which of the following?
o: Demand-pull inflation
Disinflation
Stagflation
Cost-push inflation
items.s: Stagflation is the combination of stagnant production and high joblessness with fast-rising prices.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Current account?
o: the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts
what residents earn in total after an allowance is made for the wearing out of their capital
items.s: Current account: the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts. The other options describe Net national product, Gross domestic product, Double counting.

items.q: The statement “the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels” describes which of the following?
o: Aggregation
Circular flow of income
Stabilisation policy
Macroeconomics
items.s: Stabilisation policy is the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Capital accumulation?
o: the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it
the excess of planned spending over what the economy is able to produce at full employment
the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services
the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods
items.s: Capital accumulation: the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods. The other options describe Inflationary gap, Full employment, Saving.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Multiplier.
o: rising prices caused by total spending outrunning the quantity of goods available at existing prices
a deliberate reduction in the pace of price rises that stops short of producing an outright fall
the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending
the part of that record covering movements of funds for investment and lending
items.s: Multiplier: the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending. The other options describe Demand-pull inflation, Disinflation, Capital account.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Recession?
o: a built-in feature such as a progressive tax that dampens swings in demand without any fresh decision
a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt
a deliberate reduction in the pace of price rises that stops short of producing an outright fall
a sustained fall in the general level of prices, often accompanied by falling production
items.s: Recession: a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt. The other options describe Deflation, Automatic stabiliser, Disinflation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Intermediate good?
o: an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else
the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production
a runaway rise in prices so rapid that money ceases to serve as a store of worth
the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices
items.s: Intermediate good: an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else. The other options describe Hyperinflation, Phillips curve, Expenditure approach.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Crowding out?
o: the reduction in private spending that follows when public borrowing pushes up the price of funds
a sustained fall in the general level of prices, often accompanied by falling production
a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt
the buying or selling of government securities by the monetary authority in order to alter reserves
items.s: Crowding out: the reduction in private spending that follows when public borrowing pushes up the price of funds. The other options describe Deflation, Open market operation, Recession.

items.q: The statement “the outcome in which households trying to set aside more end up with lower total earnings and no more put by” describes which of the following?
o: Paradox of thrift
Saving
Marginal propensity to consume
Consumption
items.s: Paradox of thrift is the outcome in which households trying to set aside more end up with lower total earnings and no more put by.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Potential output?
o: the quantity an economy could produce if its resources were fully and efficiently employed
the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
the buying or selling of government securities by the monetary authority in order to alter reserves
joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity
items.s: Potential output: the quantity an economy could produce if its resources were fully and efficiently employed. The other options describe Gross domestic product, Cyclical unemployment, Open market operation.

items.q: Saving may be defined as
o: the worth of output produced by the residents of a country, wherever they happen to be located
the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services
a receipt for which no good or service is given in return, such as a pension or a grant
the reduction in private spending that follows when public borrowing pushes up the price of funds
items.s: Saving: the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services. The other options describe Gross national product, Crowding out, Transfer payment.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Frictional unemployment?
o: the temporary joblessness of people moving between posts or entering work for the first time
a sustained fall in the general level of prices, often accompanied by falling production
the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending
the condition of people who are willing and able to work at going wages but cannot find it
items.s: Frictional unemployment: the temporary joblessness of people moving between posts or entering work for the first time. The other options describe Unemployment, Deflation, Multiplier.

items.q: The statement “a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending” describes which of the following?
o: Expansionary fiscal policy
Budget deficit
Fiscal policy
Public debt
items.s: Expansionary fiscal policy is a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending.

items.q: Which term is described by “the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods”?
o: Business cycle
Capital accumulation
Sustainable growth
Recession
items.s: Capital accumulation is the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Autonomous consumption?
o: the condition of people who are willing and able to work at going wages but cannot find it
the summing of many individual units into broad totals such as household spending or national production
expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests
spending that households go on undertaking even when their current earnings have fallen to nil
items.s: Autonomous consumption: spending that households go on undertaking even when their current earnings have fallen to nil. The other options describe Sustainable growth, Aggregation, Unemployment.

items.q: Which term is described by “the price of one currency expressed in terms of another”?
o: Open economy
Current account
Balance of payments
Exchange rate
items.s: Exchange rate is the price of one currency expressed in terms of another.

items.q: Disinflation may be defined as
o: the shortfall that arises when public spending in a period exceeds the revenue collected
a deliberate reduction in the pace of price rises that stops short of producing an outright fall
spending on new capital goods such as plant, machinery and buildings together with additions to stocks
a phase of rapid expansion in which demand presses hard against the capacity of the economy
items.s: Disinflation: a deliberate reduction in the pace of price rises that stops short of producing an outright fall. The other options describe Budget deficit, Investment, Boom.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Recession?
o: a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt
currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state
the price of one currency expressed in terms of another
the direct swapping of goods for goods without any common medium of payment
items.s: Recession: a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt. The other options describe Exchange rate, Legal tender, Barter.

items.q: Which term is described by “the excess of planned spending over what the economy is able to produce at full employment”?
o: Multiplier
Inflationary gap
Aggregate supply
Deflationary gap
items.s: Inflationary gap is the excess of planned spending over what the economy is able to produce at full employment.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Demand deposit?
o: a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer
the volume of production measured at the prices of a chosen standard period so that comparisons become possible
the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared
the expansion of deposits that occurs when lenders pass on a portion of what they receive
items.s: Demand deposit: a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer. The other options describe Base year, Real output, Credit creation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth”?
o: Lender of last resort
Central bank
Liquidity
Commercial bank
items.s: Liquidity is the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth.

items.q: The statement “action by the central authority to influence the cost and availability of credit and the quantity of money” describes which of the following?
o: Crowding out
Monetary policy
Fiscal policy
Expansionary fiscal policy
items.s: Monetary policy is action by the central authority to influence the cost and availability of credit and the quantity of money.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Disposable income?
o: the branch of study that examines the whole economy, its total output, total employment and general price level
what households have left to spend or set aside once direct taxes and transfers are settled
rising prices that originate in higher wages and higher input charges rather than in extra spending
the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
items.s: Disposable income: what households have left to spend or set aside once direct taxes and transfers are settled. The other options describe Cost-push inflation, Gross domestic product, Macroeconomics.

items.q: Which term is described by “the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period”?
o: Gross domestic product
Disposable income
Net national product
Transfer payment
items.s: Gross domestic product is the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period.

items.q: Which term is described by “the total stock of currency held by the public together with the deposits they keep with lenders”?
o: Fiat money
Demand deposit
Legal tender
Money supply
items.s: Money supply is the total stock of currency held by the public together with the deposits they keep with lenders.

items.q: Lender of last resort may be defined as
o: the ease with which an asset can be turned into means of payment without loss of worth
the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere
the recurring movement of activity through expansion, peak, contraction and trough
the worth of output produced by the residents of a country, wherever they happen to be located
items.s: Lender of last resort: the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere. The other options describe Liquidity, Business cycle, Gross national product.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Aggregate demand?
o: rising prices that originate in higher wages and higher input charges rather than in extra spending
the reduction in private spending that follows when public borrowing pushes up the price of funds
the institution that issues currency, holds the reserves of other lenders and acts as banker to the state
what all buyers together intend to purchase at each level of prices
items.s: Aggregate demand: what all buyers together intend to purchase at each level of prices. The other options describe Cost-push inflation, Central bank, Crowding out.

items.q: Demand deposit may be defined as
o: a sustained fall in the general level of prices, often accompanied by falling production
income that leaves the domestic flow before it is spent, as with saving, taxation and imports
a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer
the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it
items.s: Demand deposit: a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer. The other options describe Leakage, Full employment, Deflation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Legal tender.
o: a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending
a built-in feature such as a progressive tax that dampens swings in demand without any fresh decision
the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending
currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state
items.s: Legal tender: currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state. The other options describe Multiplier, Automatic stabiliser, Expansionary fiscal policy.

items.q: Which term is described by “the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it”?
o: Cyclical unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Structural unemployment
Full employment
items.s: Full employment is the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it.

items.q: The statement “the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services” describes which of the following?
o: Investment
Paradox of thrift
Saving
Depreciation
items.s: Saving is the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services.

items.q: Which term is described by “the mistaken belief that what holds for a single unit must also hold for the whole of which it is part”?
o: Stabilisation policy
Aggregation
Fallacy of composition
Leakage
items.s: Fallacy of composition is the mistaken belief that what holds for a single unit must also hold for the whole of which it is part.

items.q: Which term is described by “joblessness that arises because the skills or locations of workers no longer match the vacancies available”?
o: Cyclical unemployment
Structural unemployment
Underemployment
Frictional unemployment
items.s: Structural unemployment is joblessness that arises because the skills or locations of workers no longer match the vacancies available.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Gross domestic product?
o: a sustained rise in the general level of prices that reduces the purchasing power of money
the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
the condition of people who are willing and able to work at going wages but cannot find it
the shortfall that arises when public spending in a period exceeds the revenue collected
items.s: Gross domestic product: the market worth of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period. The other options describe Budget deficit, Unemployment, Inflation.

items.q: The statement “the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending” describes which of the following?
o: Effective demand
Multiplier
Aggregate demand
Inflationary gap
items.s: Multiplier is the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending.

items.q: The statement “a built-in feature such as a progressive tax that dampens swings in demand without any fresh decision” describes which of the following?
o: Automatic stabiliser
Budget deficit
Contractionary fiscal policy
Expansionary fiscal policy
items.s: Automatic stabiliser is a built-in feature such as a progressive tax that dampens swings in demand without any fresh decision.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Intermediate good.
o: currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state
the movement of spending and receipts between households, firms, the state and the rest of the world
an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else
improvement in living standards and in the structure of an economy, going beyond mere expansion of production
items.s: Intermediate good: an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else. The other options describe Economic development, Legal tender, Circular flow of income.

items.q: Multiplier may be defined as
o: a runaway rise in prices so rapid that money ceases to serve as a store of worth
action by the central authority to influence the cost and availability of credit and the quantity of money
the part of that record covering movements of funds for investment and lending
the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending
items.s: Multiplier: the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending. The other options describe Hyperinflation, Monetary policy, Capital account.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Expenditure approach?
o: a sustained fall in the general level of prices, often accompanied by falling production
improvement in living standards and in the structure of an economy, going beyond mere expansion of production
the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production
the role of the monetary authority in supplying funds to an institution that cannot raise them elsewhere
items.s: Expenditure approach: the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production. The other options describe Economic development, Deflation, Lender of last resort.

items.q: All of the following belong to Business cycles, growth and development EXCEPT
o: Business cycle
Recession
Boom
Saving
items.s: Every other option belongs to Business cycles, growth and development. “Saving” belongs to Consumption, saving and investment, not Business cycles, growth and development.

items.q: Exchange rate may be defined as
o: a sustained increase in the capacity of an economy to turn out goods and services over time
the price of one currency expressed in terms of another
the excess of planned spending over what the economy is able to produce at full employment
the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services
items.s: Exchange rate: the price of one currency expressed in terms of another. The other options describe Saving, Economic growth, Inflationary gap.

items.q: The statement “the shortfall in planned spending that leaves production below the level needed for full employment” describes which of the following?
o: Multiplier
Effective demand
Aggregate demand
Deflationary gap
items.s: Deflationary gap is the shortfall in planned spending that leaves production below the level needed for full employment.

items.q: Which term is described by “the volume of production measured at the prices of a chosen standard period so that comparisons become possible”?
o: Non-market production
Intermediate good
Double counting
Real output
items.s: Real output is the volume of production measured at the prices of a chosen standard period so that comparisons become possible.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Recession.
o: a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt
what households have left to spend or set aside once direct taxes and transfers are settled
improvement in living standards and in the structure of an economy, going beyond mere expansion of production
the recurring movement of activity through expansion, peak, contraction and trough
items.s: Recession: a period in which total production and joblessness worsen for long enough to be widely felt. The other options describe Disposable income, Business cycle, Economic development.

items.q: The statement “the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts” describes which of the following?
o: Open economy
Current account
Capital account
Trade balance
items.s: Current account is the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Phillips curve?
o: the expansion of deposits that occurs when lenders pass on a portion of what they receive
the fraction of an extra naira of earnings that households devote to buying goods and services
the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices
a built-in feature such as a progressive tax that dampens swings in demand without any fresh decision
items.s: Phillips curve: the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices. The other options describe Credit creation, Automatic stabiliser, Marginal propensity to consume.

items.q: Phillips curve may be defined as
o: a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending
the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods
the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices
the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it
items.s: Phillips curve: the observed trade-off in which lower joblessness goes together with faster-rising wages and prices. The other options describe Capital accumulation, Expansionary fiscal policy, Full employment.

items.q: The statement “the use of goods and services by households to satisfy their wants within a period” describes which of the following?
o: Paradox of thrift
Consumption
Investment
Saving
items.s: Consumption is the use of goods and services by households to satisfy their wants within a period.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Fiscal policy?
o: the outcome in which households trying to set aside more end up with lower total earnings and no more put by
improvement in living standards and in the structure of an economy, going beyond mere expansion of production
the use of taxation and public spending to influence total demand and the level of activity
anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth
items.s: Fiscal policy: the use of taxation and public spending to influence total demand and the level of activity. The other options describe Economic development, Money, Paradox of thrift.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Injection?
o: joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity
a sustained rise in the general level of prices that reduces the purchasing power of money
spending that enters the domestic flow from outside it, as with investment, public purchases and exports
a receipt for which no good or service is given in return, such as a pension or a grant
items.s: Injection: spending that enters the domestic flow from outside it, as with investment, public purchases and exports. The other options describe Transfer payment, Cyclical unemployment, Inflation.

items.q: Fallacy of composition may be defined as
o: currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state
the condition of people who are willing and able to work at going wages but cannot find it
the mistaken belief that what holds for a single unit must also hold for the whole of which it is part
the outcome in which households trying to set aside more end up with lower total earnings and no more put by
items.s: Fallacy of composition: the mistaken belief that what holds for a single unit must also hold for the whole of which it is part. The other options describe Paradox of thrift, Unemployment, Legal tender.

items.q: The statement “the shortfall that arises when public spending in a period exceeds the revenue collected” describes which of the following?

Expansionary fiscal policy
Budget deficit
Contractionary fiscal policy
items.s: Budget deficit is the shortfall that arises when public spending in a period exceeds the revenue collected.

items.q: The statement “rising prices caused by total spending outrunning the quantity of goods available at existing prices” describes which of the following?

Phillips curve

Demand-pull inflation

items.q: Investment may be defined as

spending on new capital goods such as plant, machinery and buildings together with additions to stocks
the shortfall that arises when public spending in a period exceeds the revenue collected
the buying or selling of government securities by the monetary authority in order to alter reserves

items.q: Expenditure approach is best described as

the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared
the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production
items.s: Expenditure approach: the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production. The other options describe Real output, Double counting, Base year.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production”?

Base year
Real output

items.q: Credit creation is best described as

the institution that issues currency, holds the reserves of other lenders and acts as banker to the state
the expansion of deposits that occurs when lenders pass on a portion of what they receive
a profit-seeking institution that takes deposits, lends them out and provides payment services

currency that circulates because the state declares it acceptable rather than because of its material worth
a balance held with a bank that its owner may withdraw on request by cheque or by transfer

the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared
the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else
items.s: Base year: the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared. The other options describe Intermediate good, Non-market production, Double counting.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Saving means.

the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services
the fraction of an extra naira of earnings that households devote to buying goods and services
spending on new capital goods such as plant, machinery and buildings together with additions to stocks
items.s: Saving: the part of current earnings that is not spent on goods and services. The other options describe Investment, Autonomous consumption, Marginal propensity to consume.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Recession means.

the skills, knowledge and health embodied in people that raise their productive capacity
the quantity an economy could produce if its resources were fully and efficiently employed

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Boom.
o: a sustained increase in the capacity of an economy to turn out goods and services over time
a phase of rapid expansion in which demand presses hard against the capacity of the economy
the recurring movement of activity through expansion, peak, contraction and trough
the skills, knowledge and health embodied in people that raise their productive capacity
items.s: Boom: a phase of rapid expansion in which demand presses hard against the capacity of the economy. The other options describe Human capital, Business cycle, Economic growth.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels”
o: Stabilisation policy
Leakage
Aggregation
Macroeconomics
items.s: Stabilisation policy is the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else”
o: Base year
Expenditure approach
Intermediate good
Real output
items.s: Intermediate good is an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else.

items.q: In this course, Expenditure approach refers to
o: an item bought by one firm from another and used up in making something else
the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item
the period whose prices serve as the standard against which production of other periods is compared
the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production
items.s: Expenditure approach: the method of adding up all spending on finished goods and services in order to arrive at total production. The other options describe Base year, Double counting, Intermediate good.

items.q: “the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts” is the definition of
o: Balance of payments
Current account
Open economy
Capital account
items.s: Current account is the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts.

items.q: The correct meaning of Fiat money is
o: the direct swapping of goods for goods without any common medium of payment
the total stock of currency held by the public together with the deposits they keep with lenders
anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth
currency that circulates because the state declares it acceptable rather than because of its material worth
items.s: Fiat money: currency that circulates because the state declares it acceptable rather than because of its material worth. The other options describe Money supply, Money, Barter.

items.q: The correct meaning of Capital accumulation is
o: expansion that can continue without exhausting the natural base on which production rests
the skills, knowledge and health embodied in people that raise their productive capacity
improvement in living standards and in the structure of an economy, going beyond mere expansion of production
the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods
items.s: Capital accumulation: the building up of the stock of machines, tools and buildings used in making goods. The other options describe Sustainable growth, Human capital, Economic development.

items.q: “a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending” is the definition of
o: Crowding out
Automatic stabiliser
Expansionary fiscal policy
Public debt
items.s: Expansionary fiscal policy is a deliberate increase in the deficit, through heavier public works or lighter taxation, meant to lift total spending.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item”
o: Double counting
Expenditure approach
Base year
Non-market production
items.s: Double counting is the error of including the same production twice, first as an input and later as a finished item.

items.q: “the shortfall in planned spending that leaves production below the level needed for full employment” is the definition of
o: Equilibrium level of income
Deflationary gap
Aggregate supply
Aggregate demand
items.s: Deflationary gap is the shortfall in planned spending that leaves production below the level needed for full employment.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state”
o: Fiat money
Money
Legal tender
Money supply
items.s: Legal tender is currency that a creditor must accept in settlement of a debt by command of the state.

items.q: “joblessness that arises because the skills or locations of workers no longer match the vacancies available” is the definition of
o: Cyclical unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Structural unemployment
Unemployment
items.s: Structural unemployment is joblessness that arises because the skills or locations of workers no longer match the vacancies available.

items.q: The correct meaning of Current account is
o: the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts
the price of one currency expressed in terms of another
the part of that record covering movements of funds for investment and lending
the difference between the worth of a country's exports and its imports of goods
items.s: Current account: the part of that record covering trade in goods and services together with unrequited receipts. The other options describe Capital account, Exchange rate, Trade balance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Aggregate supply?
o: what all buyers together intend to purchase at each level of prices
what producers together are ready to turn out and offer at each level of prices
the multiple change in total earnings that follows an initial change in autonomous spending
the shortfall in planned spending that leaves production below the level needed for full employment
items.s: Aggregate supply: what producers together are ready to turn out and offer at each level of prices. The other options describe Multiplier, Deflationary gap, Aggregate demand.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Aggregation?
o: income that leaves the domestic flow before it is spent, as with saving, taxation and imports
the branch of study that examines the whole economy, its total output, total employment and general price level
the summing of many individual units into broad totals such as household spending or national production
the movement of spending and receipts between households, firms, the state and the rest of the world
items.s: Aggregation: the summing of many individual units into broad totals such as household spending or national production. The other options describe Macroeconomics, Leakage, Circular flow of income.

items.q: The correct meaning of Money is
o: the direct swapping of goods for goods without any common medium of payment
the total stock of currency held by the public together with the deposits they keep with lenders
anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth
currency that circulates because the state declares it acceptable rather than because of its material worth
items.s: Money: anything generally accepted in payment for goods, in settlement of debt and as a store of worth. The other options describe Fiat money, Barter, Money supply.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Underemployment.
o: joblessness that arises because the skills or locations of workers no longer match the vacancies available
joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity
the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training
the condition of people who are willing and able to work at going wages but cannot find it
items.s: Underemployment: the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training. The other options describe Structural unemployment, Unemployment, Cyclical unemployment.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the movement of spending and receipts between households, firms, the state and the rest of the world”
o: Stabilisation policy
Fallacy of composition
Aggregation
Circular flow of income
items.s: Circular flow of income is the movement of spending and receipts between households, firms, the state and the rest of the world.

items.q: In this course, Stabilisation policy refers to
o: income that leaves the domestic flow before it is spent, as with saving, taxation and imports
the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels
the mistaken belief that what holds for a single unit must also hold for the whole of which it is part
the summing of many individual units into broad totals such as household spending or national production
items.s: Stabilisation policy: the deliberate use of taxing, spending and credit instruments to keep output, jobs and prices near desired levels. The other options describe Leakage, Aggregation, Fallacy of composition.

items.q: The correct meaning of Cyclical unemployment is
o: the state of people working fewer hours or in posts below their skills and training
the situation in which everyone who wants work at going wages is able to find it
the temporary joblessness of people moving between posts or entering work for the first time
joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity
items.s: Cyclical unemployment: joblessness caused by a general shortfall of spending during a downturn in activity. The other options describe Frictional unemployment, Underemployment, Full employment.
